title: fwg-world-heavyweight-2001
label: Duke tha Hammer

lost.source: WrestleSeries, 2 September 2001 (as the FWG World Triple Crown Championship, unified at License to Kill under the new N.I.W.F. ownership).

how: Duke tha Hammer beat Viper for the FWG World Heavyweight Championship, immediately unified into the World Triple Crown Championship with the N.I.W.F. Heavyweight and FWG Continental titles.
note: The title's own name changed mid-show, in-fiction, to the World Triple Crown Championship.

title: fwg-world-heavyweight-2001
label: Viper

lost.source: No later title change survives in the documents served here.

how: Beat Brick Wall (c) with the Last Ride in the WrestleSeries main event.
note: Darkside publicly challenged for a future shot at whoever won this match.

title: fwg-world-heavyweight-2001
label: Brick Wall

won.source: Not shown in the documents served here; Brick Wall is billed as the reigning World Triple Crown Champion, accompanied by Salverda, at the start of WrestleSeries on 2 September 2001.

how: Viper beat Brick Wall with the Last Ride to win the World Triple Crown Championship, with Salverda's interference backfiring.
note: How and when Brick Wall took the title from Duke tha Hammer is not attested in the documents served here.

title: fwg-cruiserweight-2001
label: Lance Dewlock

lost.source: No title change survives in the documents served here; Dewlock is still billed as champion at WrestleSeries on 2 September 2001.

how: Beat Primo Destruccion with the Final (Old Skool Expulsion).

title: fwg-deathmatch-2001
label: Darkside

lost.source: Not shown in the documents served here; Firestarter is billed as the reigning Deathmatch champion by the start of WrestleSeries on 2 September 2001, and Cowboy Underhill's own commentary there recalls Firestarter having 'won the Deathmatch title from Darkside earlier this week.'

how: Beat Hardcore G with the chokeslam to hell.
note: Darkside retained the title against Stone on the following Tuesday Rampage (20 August 2001) before losing it.

title: fwg-deathmatch-2001
label: Rio Nexan

lost.source: No later title change survives in the documents served here.

how: Beat champion Firestarter, also besting Shawn Thomas and Stain, in a brawl that spilled through a McDonald's, with the Screwed Over.

title: fwg-deathmatch-2001
label: Firestarter

won.source: Not shown in the documents served here; WrestleSeries commentary (2 September 2001) recalls Firestarter winning it from Darkside 'earlier this week.'

how: Lost a four-way (also including Shawn Thomas and Stain) to Rio Nexan's Screwed Over.

title: fwg-tag-team-2001
label: Sniper and Inferno

lost.source: No later title change survives in the documents served here.

how: Won a TLC three-way over champions Skull and Hellbound and challengers Blast and Psycho Cebo when the champions' own ladder cable gave way under Sniper and Hellbound.
note: Sniper and Inferno are billed as "former FWG Tag-team champions"; who they lost the belts to, and when, is not attested in the documents served here.

title: fwg-television-2001
label: Sheyda

lost.source: No later title change survives in the documents served here.

how: Beat champion Passion in a ladder match, unhooking the belt after Passion swept the ladder out from under her.
